info.bio: Mother Love Bone, grupo de Seattle formado por el genial Andrew Wood tras su proyecto Malfunkshun, junto con los ex-Green River Stone Gossard, Jeff Ament y Bruce Fairweather en 1988-89, fue una de las bandas pioneras de seattle. Durante esa época giraron en su ciudad, e hicieron varios tours, uno de ellos en 1989 abriendo para Dogs D'amour. Musicalmente se les puede considerar como una banda de glam-hard rock, con toques funk, pero MLB eran algo más

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Death and STP Tribute Idea (1980)
podcast.body: Andrew Wood, a member of the Seattle-based band Mother Love Bone, died of an overdose in 1980. Stone Temple Pilots had planned to dedicate their "Shangri-La Dee Da" album as a double-album tribute to him, though this elaborate concept was ultimately rejected by their record label. "This record was supposed to be a double album, something about it being a tribute to Andrew Wood of the Seattle band Mother Love Bone, who died of an overdose back in 1980."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Major Label Deal (November 1988) – Seattle Pioneers
podcast.body: In November 1988, Mother Love Bone secured a major label record deal, becoming one of the first Seattle bands to achieve this milestone. Their debut EP was well received, setting the stage for their anticipated album *Apple*. "In November 1988, Mother Love Bone became one of the first of what would be a long line of Seattle bands to nail a major label record deal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Death (March 19, 1990) – Heroin Overdose
podcast.body: Andrew Wood, the popular singer of Mother Love Bone, died on Monday, March 19, 1990, the day before their album *Apple* was due for release. He was found comatose on March 16 after a heroin overdose, and after brain activity ceased, his family chose to take him off life support. "Andrew was a really popular guy, and he had lots of friends in Seattle. His death hit Chris Cornell, his old roommate particularly hard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Frontman's Tragic Death (1990)
podcast.body: Mother Love Bone, a band described as local heroes "poised for big things," had their dreams shattered when their frontman, Andrew Wood, died of a heroin overdose. His death occurred just days before their major label album was scheduled to be released, cutting short their potential rise. "Mother Lovevone, some local heroes that were poised for big things had their dreams shot to hell when frontman Andrew Wood died of a heroin overdose just days before their major label album was supposed to come out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Cause of Death
podcast.body: The official cause of Andrew Wood's death was hypoxic encephalopathy, a condition resulting from his brain being deprived of oxygen due to him ceasing to breathe when he fell into his comatose state, causing irreversible damage. "The official cause of death was hypoxic encephalopathy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Death
podcast.body: Lead singer Andrew Wood overdosed on heroin, suffered a massive cerebral hemorrhage, and died just before the release of their debut album, "Apple." His death was a crucial event that set in motion the formation of other bands and projects like Temple of the Dog, contributing to the scene's coalescence. "Not just before that album was released, their singer Andrew Wood, overdosed on heroin, suffered a massive cerebral hemorrhage, and died."

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Death Precedes Album Release
podcast.body: Andrew Wood died only a few days before Mother Love Bone's album, "Apple," was scheduled for release. "Only a few days before the Mother Love Bone album was supposed to be released."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Death and Life Support Removal
podcast.body: Three days after being found comatose, doctors advised that there was no hope for Andrew Wood's recovery, and life support was removed. He died at 3:15 pm on Monday, March 19, 1990. "Life support was removed, and Andrew died at 3.15 pm on Monday, March 19, 1990."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Drug Overdose and Coma
podcast.body: On March 16, 1990, Andrew Wood was discovered comatose by his girlfriend after he had injected himself with heroin, leading to his hospitalization and placement on life support. "On March 16, 1990, Andrew was found comatose by his girlfriend after he'd shot himself up with heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Early Drug Use
podcast.body: Andrew Wood began smoking pot at the age of 11, and transitioned to harder drugs in his late teens, leading to multiple unsuccessful attempts at rehabilitation. "He was a pot smoker at 11. Hard drugs came along in his late teens."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Andrew Wood's Roommate at Time of Death
podcast.body: Chris Cornell was Andrew Wood's roommate at the time of his death, a detail that ties into the formation of Temple of the Dog as a tribute. "Andrew's roommate at the time he died was Chris Cornell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Disintegration after Singer's Death
podcast.body: Mother Love Bone dissolved after their singer, Andrew Wood, died from a heroin overdose. This event led Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament to seek new musical projects, eventually leading to the formation of what would become Pearl Jam. "Stone and Jeff were looking for something to do after their band Mother Love Bone fell apart when their singer Andrew Wood died of a heroin overdose."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Hiatus After Death
podcast.body: Mother Love Bone was an acclaimed Seattle band that entered a "permanent hiatus" following the overdose death of their charismatic lead singer, Andrew Wood. Pearl Jam notably rose from the ashes of this band. "Mother Lovebone, who were on permanent hiatus after the overdose death of their lead singer Andrew Wood."

podcast.title: Evolution from Malfunkshun – Group's Origin
podcast.body: Mother Love Bone developed out of an earlier group named Malfunkshun, which notably featured Greg Gilmore, a musician who had also spent time in Skinyard with Jack Endino and Daniel House. "They had evolved out of malfunction, a group featuring a dude named Greg Gilmore, who, for a time, had been in Skinyard with Jack and Dino and Daniel House."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Legacy and Band Spin-offs
podcast.body: Following Andrew Wood's death, the surviving members, bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard, along with friends from Soundgarden, formed Temple of the Dog to record a memorial album. The positive experience of these sessions eventually led Ament and Gossard to form Pearl Jam. "Some of the surviving members of Mother Love Bone got together with friends from Soundgarden, a few other local musicians to record an album in Andrew's memory."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Major Label Ambitions
podcast.body: Mother Love Bone actively sought to become successful rock stars and achieve a major label deal, which they eventually secured with Mercury Records. This contrasted with the uncommercial nature of some early grunge bands. "Mother Love Bone wanted to be successful. They wanted to be rock and roll stars. They wanted a major label deal, and they got it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Manager Kelly Curtis's Distraction
podcast.body: Kelly Curtis, who initially co-managed Alice in Chains, became distracted by the growing popularity of Mother Love Bone, his other management client. This distraction led to Susan Silver taking on more day-to-day responsibilities for Alice in Chains.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Precursor to Pearl Jam
podcast.body: The "fallout" from Mother Love Bone directly led to the formation of Pearl Jam. "And then there was the Fallout from Mother Love Bone, which eventually resulted in the formation of Pearl Jam, who also went right to a major."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tragic Death of Andrew Wood
podcast.body: Three weeks before the scheduled release of their debut album, "Apple," Mother Love Bone's singer Andrew Wood died from a heroin overdose. This tragedy led to the formation of Temple of the Dog as a tribute and subsequently, Pearl Jam. "Three weeks before it comes out, singer Andrew Wood dies of a heroin overdose."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transformation into Pearl Jam – Post-Tragedy Rebirth
podcast.body: Following the tragic death of Andrew Wood, the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, collaborated with Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron to form Temple of the Dog. This collaboration eventually led Ament and Gossard to form a new band with Eddie Vedder, initially called Mookie Blaylock, which soon became Pearl Jam. "When Mother Lovebone collapsed and turned into Pearl Jam, Kelly became their full-time manager, leaving Susan to deal with Allison Chains."

xref.title: "Trajik Love Company" Name Origin
xref.body: The name "Trajik Love Company" was an amalgamation of the band's three favorite groups: The Tragically Hip, Mother Love Bone, and Bad Company. "The name Trajik Love Company was an amalgamation of the band's three favorite groups, the Trajik Lee Hip, mother Love Bone, and bad company."

xref.title: Andrew Wood Memorial
xref.body: Temple of the Dog was a Seattle supergroup formed specifically to record an album in memory of Andrew Wood, the singer of Mother Love Bone, who died of a heroin overdose. The project brought together surviving members of Mother Love Bone and friends from Soundgarden. "Some of the surviving members of Mother Love Bone got together with friends from Soundgarden, a few other local musicians to record an album in Andrew's memory. They called their Seattle group Temple of the Dog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Catalyst for Pearl Jam
xref.body: The musicians who participated in the Temple of the Dog recording sessions enjoyed their time together, leading Mother Love Bone's bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard to decide to continue working together, eventually forming Pearl Jam with Mike McCready and Eddie Vedder. "Most of the musicians who took part in the Temple of the Dog Sessions really had a good time hanging out. And when the record was finished, Mother Love Bone's bassist and guitarist decided to stick together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Co-Manager of Alice in Chains – Partnership with Kelly Curtis
xref.body: Susan Silver co-managed Alice in Chains with Kelly Curtis through their shared management company. When Mother Love Bone collapsed and transformed into Pearl Jam, Kelly Curtis shifted his focus to become Pearl Jam's full-time manager, leaving Susan to manage Alice in Chains independently. "When Mother Lovebone started to get hot, Kelly wanted to spend more time with them. Meanwhile, Ken wanted out, so Susan and Kelly became co-managers of Allison Chains through their own management company."

xref.title: Early Co-Management and Susan Silver's Involvement
xref.body: Alice in Chains was initially co-managed by Kelly Curtis. When Curtis became distracted by the growing popularity of his other band, Mother Love Bone, Susan Silver took over much of the day-to-day management for Alice in Chains. It was Silver who secured their record deal.

xref.title: Early Seattle Band – Brief Stone Gossard Connection
xref.body: March of Crimes was a band in Seattle that featured Ben Shepherd, who would later become Soundgarden's bassist. Notably, a teenage Stone Gossard, future member of Mother Love Bone and Pearl Jam, briefly played guitar in this group. "Ben had been around Seattle for years, once playing in a band called March of Crimes, which briefly featured a teenage guitarist named Stone Gossard."

xref.title: Formation and Major Label Debut
xref.body: Pearl Jam was formed as a result of the fallout from the band Mother Love Bone, and they proceeded to sign directly with a major label. Jeff Ament, a member of Green River, was a part of this formation. "And then there was the Fallout from Mother Love Bone, which eventually resulted in the formation of Pearl Jam, who also went right to a major."

xref.title: Formation as a Tribute
xref.body: Temple of the Dog was formed as a one-time-only band specifically as a tribute to Andrew Wood, who was Chris Cornell's roommate and a member of Mother Love Bone. "And as a tribute, he formed a one-time only band called Temple of the Dog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation from Mother Love Bone and Temple of the Dog
xref.body: Pearl Jam was formed by Mother Love Bone's bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard, who decided to continue playing together after the Temple of the Dog sessions. They were joined by guitarist Mike McCready, a veteran of several small Seattle groups, and singer Eddie Vedder, who had moved from San Diego to perform background vocals on the Temple of the Dog record. "Jeff Ammett and Stone Gossard were joined by guitarist Mike McCready, a veteran of several small Seattle groups. And for a singer, they chose this skinny surfer dude who had moved up from San Diego to do background vocals on the Temple of the Dog record. His name was Eddie Vetter and the result of course was Pearl Jam."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Predecessor to Mother Love Bone – Early Band
xref.body: Malfunkshun was an earlier musical group from which Mother Love Bone evolved. The band featured a musician named Greg Gilmore, who also had connections to Skinyard. "They had evolved out of malfunction, a group featuring a dude named Greg Gilmore, who, for a time, had been in Skinyard with Jack and Dino and Daniel House."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Predecessor to Pearl Jam – Formation with Eddie Vedder
xref.body: Mookie Blaylock was the original name of the band formed by Mother Love Bone's Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, who invited a young singer named Eddie Vedder from San Diego to join. The band quickly changed its name to Pearl Jam, which went on to achieve massive success. "This kid from San Diego who had just flown up at the invitation of Jeff and Stone to sing in a new band that was going to be called Mookie Blaylock, and that kid's name was Eddie Vedder."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Roommate of Andrew Wood – Impact on Temple of the Dog
xref.body: Chris Cornell shared an apartment with Andrew Wood, the singer of Mother Love Bone. Wood's unexpected death in March 1990 profoundly affected Cornell, leading him to write songs in tribute that eventually formed the basis of the Temple of the Dog project. "Andrew died the day Chris got back from a long tour with Soundgarden. A few days after the funeral, Chris and Soundgarden headed out on a European tour, and while on the road, Chris started running some songs in tribute to his old friend."

xref.title: Tribute to Andrew Wood
xref.body: Temple of the Dog was formed as a quick tribute to Andrew Wood, Chris Cornell's former roommate and the singer of Mother Love Bone, who tragically died in March 1990. Cornell wrote several songs in his friend's honor, which he then shared with the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, leading to the formation of this supergroup. "When he got back to Seattle, he showed the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, the songs. When other materials started flowing, they decided to record a quick tribute album under the name Temple of the Dog."
